articles.title: Bill Maher Fires Back at Trump by Comparing Him to Taylor Swift
articles.summary: Bill Maher learned that when it comes to Donald Trump, no good deed goes unpunished. On last week’s episode of “Real Time with Bill Maher,” the political pundit defended his recent White House dinner with the president, exclaiming, “You know what? Fuck you.
body: Well, Maher took the stage of “Real Time” Friday night and, before welcoming Ted Cruz and the aforementioned Kid Rock as guests, wasted no time addressing that incredibly long Trump rant.

“Did you see the 1,300-word [Truth Social post] he sent out? Longest ever! Kind of a flex,” offered Maher during his monologue. “I tell ya, dining at the White House is the opposite of the Cheesecake Factory — after you leave, they review you!”

“He went off on me like Kelly Clarkson in a toy store,” he continued. “Eating with Trump is like dating Taylor Swift: It’s a lot of laughs at the time, but later on, they’re tearing you a new asshole.”

Maher wasn’t finished: “Look, I don’t want it to be this way. The whole point of having these dinners was talk, disagree but listen — which he does, in person — but don’t hate each other, I go back to my job here and the heartaches begin. I’m not going to refute everything, but I do have to address a few of the allegations.”

body: Martin Scorsese ‘s “ Cleopatra ” never came to fruition, and he says the Angelina Jolie -starrer was nixed because of Seth Rogen and the Sony hack.
According to Scorsese, this caused some aftereffects in the industry, which he described in the first episode of the Tribeca original series “ Crafty.”

“We were gonna do Cleopatra at one point, and then they made fun of [Kim Jong Un], and he got mad and blew up everybody at Columbia,” Scorsese said. “Seth Rogen, right? And then he got mad, and [it] ruined Cleopatra.”

Though Rogen wasn’t directly responsible for the project being canceled, the resulting hack exposed thousands of emails, including ones from producer Scott Rudin to Sony’s Amy Pascal calling Jolie “a minimally talented spoiled brat.”

articles.title: Daytime Emmys 2026 Winners List (UPDATED LIVE)
articles.summary: The 53rd Daytime Emmys are underway at Hollywood’s historic Palladium theatre. CBS’ “The Young and the Restless” led all programs with 18 nods this year, followed by new CBS soap opera “Beyond the Gates” — which In its first year of eligibility scored 15 nominations.
body: Among soaps, “Beyond the Gates” burst out of the gates in its first year with four wins, including for lead actress in a drama (Tamara Tunie, winning her first-ever Emmy), emerging talent in a daytime drama series (for Ambyr Michelle), lighting direction and hairstyling/makeup.
“This is the best ‘welcome back to daytime’ ever,” said Tunie, who first began working in the genre in 1987.

“Young and the Restless” wins included supporting actor in a drama winner Roger Howarth (“The Young and the Restless”), who made Daytime Emmy history for the longest gap between wins (it’s been 32 years since he last won a Daytime Emmy). The show also won for supporting actress in a daytime drama (Beth Maitland).

“General Hospital” also has three so far, including for writing team and for guest performer in a daytime drama (Jeff Kober, who also earned a Primetime Emmy nomination this year for “The Pitt,” a rare double nomination for both awards shows in the same year).

articles.title: Two Arrested in Murder of ‘SNL’ Writer’s Sister
articles.summary: Two suspects have been arrested in connection with the murder of Christina Downer, “Saturday Night Live” writer Jimmy Fowlie’s sister, according to the Los Angeles Police Department.
body: Downer was reported missing after a welfare check on Dec. 18, 2025, and Brandon claimed she had moved out and left behind her car and dog.

LAPD said law enforcement officials continued to investigate Downer’s disappearance after her cell phone washed ashore on the beach in Santa Monica. Authorities were led to search an Airbnb property in Joshua Tree, located in the high desert several hours from Los Angeles, in connection with her disappearance and conducted an extensive search with K-9 units and the San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department.

articles.title: Celebrity Traitors comes to a climax in nail-biting final
articles.summary: The second series of the hit show reached its climax on Friday after attracting 15 million viewers.
body: We've had four weeks of suspense, suspicion and very suspect tactics, as some of Britain's biggest stars engaged in a battle of wits to win the most popular show on TV.
The second series of BBC One's The Celebrity Traitors reached its climax on Friday, with the 21 original contestants having been reduced to seven before the final.
They were then whittled down to two winners - with the faithful duo of comedian Romesh Ranganathan and Heartstopper actor Sebastian "Bash" Croft emerging victorious.
The players successfully banished the remaining traitors - Love Island host Maya Jama and YouTuber King Kenny - in dramatic fashion, and the winning pair shared the £83,000 prize for their charities.

articles.title: How Bristol shaped Maya Jama before her TV fame
articles.summary: The Love Island host's journey from leaving Bristol as a teenager to reaching the BBC show's finale.
body: Maya Jama has gone from Bristol schoolgirl to one of the UK's biggest television stars.
The 32-year-old Love Island host was watched by millions as she faced the last round table in the final of The Celebrity Traitors, which aired on BBC One and iPlayer.
But behind the glamorous television appearances and red carpet moments is a story that began in a council house with a young girl determined to make it on the small screen.
Maya was born and raised in Bristol, growing up in St Paul's with a family of Bristol Rovers supporters, putting on song and dance performances for them and charging 20p a time.

articles.title: Timbaland Files $15 Million Fraud Lawsuit Against Former Managers
articles.summary: The super-producer alleges that former manager Gary Marella and business manager Bruce Seckendorf "used their entrusted authority to enrich themselves and others, conceal financial misconduct, and deplete Timbaland’s valuable assets."
body: Timbaland has filed a $15 million lawsuit against his former manager and business manager, accusing the two executives of fraud, breach of fiduciary duty and civil theft, among other claims.
The former business manager Bruce Seckendorf, Timbaland, whose real name is Timothy Mosley, alleges, “failed to pay Mosley’s mortgage and allowed his home to reach the brink of foreclosure.”

The suit claims Seckendorf’s firm “failed to timely pay substantial federal taxes, causing millions in penalties and interest, while continuing to pay themselves, the Marella Defendants, and other professionals millions in commissions, fees, and purported loan repayments.”

Per the suit, Timbaland only learned of the alleged misconduct because he got a foreclosure notice at his home last year. After receiving the notice, the suit says, Timbaland called Seckendorf, who the producer says failed to “clearly explain why his office had failed to make the mortgage payments without informing Mosley.”

articles.title: Party Rock Anthem singer struggled with mental health before death
articles.summary: Lauren Bennett, who featured on LMFAO's hit song, was found dead by her husband.
body: A British singer who was a member of the girl group G.R.L took her own life, an inquest has found.
Lauren Bennett, 36, who also featured on LMFAO's 2011 hit Party Rock Anthem, was found dead in Kent on 29 May.
In a statement read out by an assistant coroner on Friday, her husband Kenny Wormald said she had been struggling with severe mental health issues before her death.
The court heard she told him she was going out for a walk on the morning of her death while he remained in bed half asleep.

articles.title: Sir Patrick Stewart remembered as 'Mirfield's finest'
articles.summary: Tributes have been paid to the legendary Star Trek actor Sir Patrick Stewart, who was born in Mirfield.
body: Sir Patrick Stewart once said he had to drop his Yorkshire accent for Hollywood, but he never forgot his roots.

The Mirfield-born actor, best known for his roles in Star Trek and the X-Men films, died at the age of 86 at his home in Los Angeles on Wednesday after suffering with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.
His death has prompted an outpouring of love from the community he proudly called home, along with his beloved Huddersfield Town - the club he followed from childhood.
Stewart's friend and fellow legendary actor Sir Ian McKellen said Stewart "never forsook his origins".

articles.title: The Hollywood Reporter Wins 2026 Daytime Emmy Award
articles.summary: This was the third consecutive nomination for the 'Off Script' roundtable series, which has received a total of six nods over the past nine years.
body: The Hollywood Reporter ‘s Off Script roundtable series has won its first Daytime Emmy Award.

The awards -season showcase was recognized at the 2026 Daytime Emmys Friday night, where it won in the arts and popular culture category after receiving its third consecutive nomination. In total, the series has garnered six Daytime Emmy nominations since 2017.

Off Script is the magazine’s iconic roundtable series, which has aired on IFC, streaming on AMC+, over the past three years. The series consists of five episodes of Emmy contenders: drama actress, drama actor, comedy actress, comedy actor and stand-up.

Rabishaw thanked the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences “for the recognition” and praised the fellow nominees in the category, “including our sister brand Variety, which was nominated twice.”

articles.title: Selma Blair Apologizes for Plane Arrest: “Not One Day Have I Intended to Hurt or Frighten Anyone”
articles.summary: The actress was arrested at John F. Kennedy International Airport on Oct. 11 after an alleged incident on a Delta plane that resulted in two flight attendants being injured and one being sent to the hospital.
body: Selma Blair is apologizing for her Oct. 11 plane arrest, where she allegedly assaulted two flight attendants onboard a Delta Los Angeles-New York flight.

“Hi. It’s me, and I know I’ve been quiet for a couple of weeks since October 11th, and you deserve to hear from me directly, and I’m sorry that it’s taken this long,” the actress said in an Instagram video Friday. “There is a legal matter going on, and my lawyers have asked me to not say anything about that day, and I’m listening to them. And I take this very seriously.”

The Legally Blonde star noted that “what I can tell you though is very simple, and the truest thing I know about myself [is] that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone, a day in my life.” She continued, “And so to the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, that I frightened, alarmed; I am so sorry.” Related Stories.
